_about: The medallion pipeline: its batch flow on the flow's terms (release 1) and its design (release 2): the classes of the specification's steps D1 to D7 and D9, and how the flow executes them. Names follow DECISIONS.md.
_summary: A medallion data pipeline, source systems to bronze, silver and gold: its sources, reference data, conformed entities, gold outputs and contracts, derivation and quality rules, build plan, and the batch flow that executes them, with the rules a design and a declared flow must satisfy.
name: Medallion pipeline

SourceSystem.definition: A system the pipeline reads from, and how: its kind, the access method, whether filters may run on its side (D2).

SourceTable.definition: One table or feed of a source system, with its contract: keys, the column a row's date is in, how it changes over time and the evidence for it, when it arrives (D2).

SourceColumn.definition: A column of a source table: its name, source type, nullability and unit, and the business term it carries (D2, D3).

CopyPolicy.definition: How a source table reaches bronze: a period slice, new rows by watermark, an as-of read or a change feed; the lookback, the source-side filter, the retention (D2).

TermMapping.definition: How a source column becomes a business term: the transform from the source form to the canonical one (D3).

CodeSet.definition: A list of allowed values with their labels per published language (D3).

CodeMapping.definition: Which value of a source system means which canonical value of a code set (D3).

ConformedEntity.definition: A silver business entity, resolved once across sources: its grain, how each source's id maps to its key, which instances are in scope, how history is kept, the table it is materialised as (D4). The specification's Entity, renamed (DECISIONS.md).

IdentityMapping.definition: How one source table's id becomes the conformed key: the id columns, their transform, the target key fields (D4).

ScopeRule.definition: Which instances of an entity are in scope, how many there should be, by whose count, and how far off the count may be (D4).

HistoryPolicy.definition: Whether an entity keeps history, and how: none, a snapshot per batch, or validity ranges (D4).

Dataset.definition: A physical table or view of the pipeline, in one layer, with its grain, partitioning and fields (D4, D5). The specification's Table, renamed; a kind of DataStore, so it runs in an environment and has an owner.

DatasetField.definition: A field of a dataset: its type, whether it is required, the business term it carries, and either the rule that derives it or what feeds it (D4, D5). The specification's Field, renamed.

Output.definition: A gold dataset a consumer reads: its shape, the silver entity it is keyed on, whether it needs a window of periods, the data product it belongs to (D5).

DataContract.definition: A versioned shape of a dataset others depend on: its fields, keys and change policy (D5). A kind of Interface: consumers consume it, a version supersedes the one before it, it has an owner.

DerivationRule.definition: How one field is produced, or rows are filtered: its kind, its logic as a pattern of the vocabulary, its inputs, its behaviour on the standard edge cases, and an example (D6). The specification's Rule, renamed.

EdgeCase.definition: What a derivation rule does on one edge case: a tie, a null input, missing history, an entity younger than the lookback, a duplicate input (D6).

RuleExample.definition: One real input and the output a derivation rule must give for it, worked out by someone other than the generating agent (D6).

QualityRule.definition: What must be true of the data at one gate (1 landing to bronze, 2 bronze to silver, 3 silver to gold): its targets, its assertion, hard or soft, its tolerance, what happens when it fails, a row that should fail it (D7). Carried out by a flow check on the gate's step.

Tolerance.definition: How far off a count or a figure may be, in which unit, set by whom (D4, D7).

FailureAction.definition: What happens when a quality rule fails: who is told, which runbook they follow, whether the step retries (D7).

Identity.definition: A principal the pipeline runs as or a person who reads it: its kind, the environment, its access to datasets (D9).

delivered_by.label: delivered by
delivered_by.definition: The system the table comes from.

has_key.label: has key
has_key.definition: A column that identifies a row of the table.

date_column.label: date column
date_column.definition: The column that says what date a row is about.

has_column.label: has column
has_column.definition: A column the pipeline reads from the table.

watermark.label: watermark
watermark.definition: For an incremental copy: the column that is the watermark.

stewarded_by.label: stewarded by
stewarded_by.definition: The role that answers for it: who answers questions about a source table, defines a term, owns a code set or a quality rule.

carries_term.label: carries term
carries_term.definition: The business term a column or a field carries.

term_code_set.label: code set
term_code_set.definition: The list a term takes its values from.

maps_column.label: maps column
maps_column.definition: The source column a term mapping reads.

maps_to.label: maps to
maps_to.definition: The business term a term mapping produces.

of_code_set.label: of code set
of_code_set.definition: The code set a code mapping maps into.

from_system.label: from system
from_system.definition: The source system whose value a code mapping maps.

has_identity_mapping.label: has identity mapping
has_identity_mapping.definition: How one source's id becomes the entity's key.

scoped_by.label: scoped by
scoped_by.definition: Which instances of the entity count.

materialised_as.label: materialised as
materialised_as.definition: The table an entity or an output is.

from_table.label: from table
from_table.definition: The source table whose id an identity mapping maps.

id_column.label: id column
id_column.definition: A column that holds the source id.

target_key.label: target key
target_key.definition: A key field of the entity the source id maps to.

within_tolerance.label: within tolerance
within_tolerance.definition: How far off a count or a figure may be.

grain.label: grain
grain.definition: A field of the grain: one row per what.

bound_to.label: bound to
bound_to.definition: The code set a field's values come from.

derived_by.label: derived by
derived_by.definition: The rule that computes the field.

fed_by.label: fed by
fed_by.definition: What a copied field comes from. If this changes, what is fed by it is affected, transitively.

output_of.label: output of
output_of.definition: The data product the output belongs to.

joins_to.label: joins to
joins_to.definition: The silver entity the output is keyed on.

reads_output.label: reads output
reads_output.definition: A role or a persona who reads the output; a tool, an API or a downstream pipeline is a System that consumes its contract.

contract_of.label: contract of
contract_of.definition: The dataset whose shape the contract promises.

rule_input.label: rule input
rule_input.definition: A field or a column the rule reads.

has_edge_case.label: has edge case
has_edge_case.definition: The rule's behaviour on one edge case.

has_example.label: has example
has_example.definition: An example that proves the rule.

targets.label: targets
targets.definition: A dataset or a field the rule checks.

failure_action.label: failure action
failure_action.definition: What happens when the rule fails.

carried_out_by.label: carried out by
carried_out_by.definition: The flow check, on its gate's step, that runs the rule.

set_by.label: set by
set_by.definition: The role that set the tolerance.

notifies.label: notifies
notifies.definition: The role told when the rule fails.

follows_runbook.label: follows runbook
follows_runbook.definition: The runbook the notified role follows.

executes.label: executes
executes.definition: What a step of a medallion flow runs: a copy policy, an entity's build, an output's build, a derivation rule. The specification's Transformation is the step itself (DECISIONS.md).

represents.label: represents
represents.definition: The design table an artifact of the flow is: a dataset, or a source table.

in_environment.label: in environment
in_environment.definition: The environment an identity belongs to.

resumes_from.label: resumes from
resumes_from.definition: The step a recovery resumes the flow from.

layer.label: layer
layer.definition: The layer a table of the pipeline sits in: a source read from outside, bronze (copied as is), silver (conformed), gold (what consumers read), or control (the batch's own records).

gate.label: gate
gate.definition: For a run_gate step, the boundary it checks: 1 landing to bronze, 2 bronze to silver, 3 silver to gold.

period_kind.label: period kind
period_kind.definition: How often a period of the data product closes.

period_end_rule.label: period end rule
period_end_rule.definition: What date ends a period: calendar_month_end, last_business_day, fixed_day: N, or event.

freshness_sla.label: freshness SLA
freshness_sla.definition: By when, after the period ends, gold must be ready (a duration).

data_type.label: data type
data_type.definition: The canonical type of the term's values.

unit.label: unit
unit.definition: The canonical unit, when the term is a quantity (percent, fraction, cents…).

source_kind.label: source kind
source_kind.definition: What kind of system the source is.

source_side_logic_allowed.label: source-side logic allowed
source_side_logic_allowed.definition: Whether filters may run on the source side; never business logic.

schema.label: schema
schema.definition: The schema, as the source names it.

table_name.label: table name
table_name.definition: The table or feed name, as the source names it.

change_behaviour.label: change behaviour
change_behaviour.definition: How the table changes over time.

change_behaviour_evidence.label: change behaviour evidence
change_behaviour_evidence.definition: What proves the change behaviour: a drift measurement or the owner's statement.

expected_at_period_end.label: expected at period end
expected_at_period_end.definition: Whether it must have rows for the period end before a batch runs.

delivery_lag.label: delivery lag
delivery_lag.definition: How long after the period end it arrives (a duration).

column_name.label: column name
column_name.definition: The column name, as the source names it.

source_type.label: source type
source_type.definition: The column's type in the source.

unit.label: unit
unit.definition: For a number: its unit in the source (percent, fraction, cents…).

sample_values.label: sample values
sample_values.definition: Three real values, for the fixtures.

lookback.label: lookback
lookback.definition: How far before the period end rows are needed (a duration).

source_side_filter.label: source-side filter
source_side_filter.definition: The filter that runs on the source, if any: date_between(period_end - lookback, period_end).

retention_hot.label: hot retention
retention_hot.definition: How long bronze keeps it in hot storage.

transform.label: transform
transform.definition: From source form to canonical: identity, rename, trim, upper, lower, lpad: N, char, divide: N, multiply: N, to_date: format, to_utc: tz, code_map: set, coalesce: [a, b, default].

labels.label: labels
labels.definition: Each value's label in each published language, as value@language: label.

source_value.label: source value
source_value.definition: The value as the source system writes it.

canonical_value.label: canonical value
canonical_value.definition: The code set's value it means.

transform.label: transform
transform.definition: How the source id is normalised (a transform pattern).

company_or_tenant_map.label: company or tenant map
company_or_tenant_map.definition: When a company or tenant code is part of the key: source=canonical pairs.

conditions.label: conditions
conditions.definition: What makes an instance in scope: field operator value, with =, !=, in, not_in, is_null, is_not_null, exists_in.

expected_count.label: expected count
expected_count.definition: How many instances there should be.

count_as_of.label: count as of
count_as_of.definition: The date the expected count holds.

count_source.label: count source
count_source.definition: Who or what says the count.

history_kind.label: history kind
history_kind.definition: No history, one snapshot per batch, or validity ranges.

valid_from_rule.label: valid-from rule
valid_from_rule.definition: For scd2: how a range's start is derived.

valid_to_rule.label: valid-to rule
valid_to_rule.definition: For scd2: how a range's end is derived.

layer.label: layer
layer.definition: The layer the dataset is in.

dataset_kind.label: dataset kind
dataset_kind.definition: A physical table or a view.

partition_by.label: partition by
partition_by.definition: The partition key: batch_id for the data layers.

cluster_by.label: cluster by
cluster_by.definition: The fields it is clustered by.

required.label: required
required.definition: Whether every row has a value.

shape.label: shape
shape.definition: Long (one row per key, dimension and value) unless the consumer cannot read long.

period_dependency.label: period dependency
period_dependency.definition: Whether it needs only the period or a window.

lookback.label: lookback
lookback.definition: How far back, when it needs a window.

needs_history.label: needs history
needs_history.definition: Whether a consumer reads past periods, not only the current one.

contract_fields.label: fields
contract_fields.definition: The promised fields, in order, as name: type, required or optional.

keys.label: keys
keys.definition: The fields that identify a row.

change_policy.label: change policy
change_policy.definition: Whether columns may be added without a new version.

rule_kind.label: rule kind
rule_kind.definition: What kind of rule it is.

logic.label: logic
logic.definition: How, exactly: a pattern of the vocabulary (copy, rank_by, sum_by, latest_by, window_from_returns, ratio, std_dev_over, case, filter, join_lookup) with its parameters, or expression: <text> with reviewed_by.

reviewed_by.label: reviewed by
reviewed_by.definition: Who signed off a free-form expression.

period_dependency.label: period dependency
period_dependency.definition: Whether the rule depends on the period.

lookback.label: lookback
lookback.definition: How far back, when it needs a window.

specified_in.label: specified in
specified_in.definition: The section of the specification the rule comes from.

behaviour.label: behaviour
behaviour.definition: What happens: exclude, include_as: value, error, first_by: field, last_by: field, carry_forward, or prose with reviewed_by.

inputs.label: inputs
inputs.definition: The input rows, or the fixture that holds them.

expected_output.label: expected output
expected_output.definition: The rows that must come out, or the fixture that holds them.

computed_by.label: computed by
computed_by.definition: Who worked out the expected value; never the generating agent.

rule_id.label: rule id
rule_id.definition: The rule's identifier, cited by the check that carries it out.

gate.label: gate
gate.definition: The boundary it runs at: 1 landing to bronze, 2 bronze to silver, 3 silver to gold.

assertion.label: assertion
assertion.definition: What must be true: a pattern (present_for_period, fresh, schema_matches, count_within, unique, not_null, in_set, mapped, references, count_equals, not_after, in_range, sum_to, change_within, covered, consistent, long_form) with its parameters, or expression: <predicate> with reviewed_by.

example_failure.label: example failure
example_failure.definition: A row, or the fixture holding it, that should fail the rule.

specified_in.label: specified in
specified_in.definition: The section of the specification the rule comes from.

auto_retry.label: auto retry
auto_retry.definition: Whether the step retries by itself.

max_retries.label: maximum retries
max_retries.definition: How many times, when it does.

identity_kind.label: identity kind
identity_kind.definition: A service principal or a person.

access.label: access
access.definition: Its access, as layer: mode (bronze: read, silver: write…).
